item.title: Tennis Channel gatekeeping WTA World No. 1 Elena Rybakina Ningbo Open SF behind paywall
item.description: The fall Asian swing has been a bit of a snoozer for both the WTA and ATP tennis tours. Fans are hard pressed to find many matches that elicit excitement or merit the energy to get up early in the morning on the East Coast to watch live. Saturday finally gave us one, it is the Ningbo Open semifinal match between WTA World No. 1 Elena Rybakina and Diana Shnaider. However, it is not on Tennis Channel; apparently, streaming it with the TC paid subscription service is the only way to watch it. The subscription costs $11.99 per month or $109 per year. That’s another baffling decision because there is a dedicated pickleball channel. However, Stefanos Tsitsipas’s match at the ATP 250 Almaty Open is not as much of a crowd pleaser. This is no slight on Tsitsipas who is a former ATP World No. 3, but his opponent is outside the Top 100. Besides, a 250-level tournament is not as important as the 500-level one at Ningbo. But the KC metro is experiencing a golf renaissance. The game is booming just as it is in most U.S. regions, and club owners and municipalities alike are investing big dollars in their properties, crafting elite golf experiences for members and residents while also attracting golfers from around the country. It’s quite rare these days to see a municipality invest the money needed to totally overhaul a golf course, but COVID spurred an unprecedented boom in the golf industry, and the game continues to grow beyond its initial pandemic bump. Even so, trying to convince a city to spend millions on a golf course is often a losing battle. It wasn’t for Schroeder, though, as everyone involved seemed to agree that Swope needed a major facelift. Public golfers now reap the benefits of a pristine course that will charge a reasonable $84 for a weekend round with other tee times available for as low as $38 for walking weekday seniors. Read the full story behind the renovation project at Swope Memorial. Oakwood Country Club About 10 miles south of downtown KC, on the Missouri side, you’ll find the oldest golf club in the city. Oakwood Country Club was founded in 1881 as the Progress Club, designed as a social hangout for Jewish children and families. Thirty years later, legendary architect Tom Bendelow was hired to construct the first nine holes of the golf course, with the second nine built in 1923. Throughout its history, the course has undergone several changes, including in 1991 when PGA Tour legend Tom Watson helped redesign four holes on the front nine. Its synthetic turf tees are a brilliant concept that not only give players a perfect lie to spin the ball on all nine shots, it saves the club hours of labor and expenses while avoiding extensive tree maintenance. Over the years, she’s become known as a tenacious rebounder who just cannot score consistently or efficiently. That’s not the player we saw this season, especially down the stretch. This season, Reese averaged a career-high 16.4 points per game, shot 45.1% from the field, and added 2.8 assists per game. And that’s come with some dominant scoring totals. Against the Sparks earlier this year, Reese went a perfect 9-for-9 from the field for 20 points and then followed that up with a career-high 31 points the following game. And she’s been even better on the biggest stage. In Game 2 of the WNBA Finals, with Atlanta needing a road win over Golden State to help swing the momentum in the series, Reese had perhaps the best game of her entire career as she was dominant on both sides of the court. She finished the game with 30 points – one shy of the career-high she set earlier in the season – along with 16 rebounds, 2 blocks, 3 assists, and one steal while only turning the ball over twice. For most of her career, Reese has been a liability on offense. This season, into the postseason, she’s been one of the most reliable players on the court. Clark’s Weaknesses To be clear, Clark had a terrific offensive season. In fact, it was one of the best in WNBA history. She averaged 22.3 points and 8.3 assists per game and became the first player in WNBA history with at least 800 points and 300 assists in a single season. She also finished fourth in MVP voting. But Clark’s defense continues to be a problem. Early in the season, she faced more isolation plays on defense than any other player in the league, according to Sporting News . In the season opener alone, the Dallas Wings went right at her , scoring 25 points on 9-of-12 shooting with Clark as the primary defender. Beyond simply giving up points on the defensive end, Clark’s defensive woes have another impact – keeping her off the court. In several games this season, opponents were able to get Clark in foul trouble early, resulting in her spending large chunks of the game on the bench. In games where this happens, the time on the bench makes it nearly impossible for her to get into a rhythm offensively, and ultimately hurts the team on the offensive end, too. “I know I have to improve in that area,” Clark admitted earlier this season. While Clark is undeniably one of the best scorers and passers in the league, her offense isn’t without flaws. Clark led the WNBA with 183 turnovers this season, including a league-high 120 live-ball turnovers that led to 105 fast-break points for opponents. She’s actually led the league in turnovers in each of her three seasons in the league. And while she can catch fire from deep, the nature of her game lends itself to cold stretches, like a two-game span in June when she shot 4-of-19 from the field. Sometimes, those cold streaks come at rather inopportune times for the Fever, like her historically poor performance in the regular season finale against the Minnesota Lynx – a loss which ultimately cost Indiana home-court advantage in the first round of the postseason and solidified a matchup with the defending champion Las Vegas Aces in the opening round. The Fever were bounced in the first round by the Las Vegas Aces, and Clark admitted that “we could’ve put ourselves in a better spot going into the postseason,” via the Associated Press . Two-Way Star None of this is to say that Clark isn’t a great player. She is, and she remains the biggest draw in the sport by a wide margin, and she was an MVP candidate throughout the season for a reason. But when it comes to impact and consistency on both sides of the court, Reese now does more things at an elite level. She’s the league’s best rebounder, its Defensive Player of the Year, and a reliable scorer, and she’s the one still playing in late October. Clearly, the gap between the two has closed. item.title: How will Arsenal survive two months without Saka?
item.description: How will Arsenal survive two months without Saka? Arsenal have reportedly suffered a significant setback, with Bukayo Saka expected to miss up to eight weeks after sustaining a fresh injury . The winger has been an important figure in the Gunners’ campaign so far, and his absence could create problems for Mikel Arteta as the club continues its bid to retain the Premier League title. Saka made a strong start to the season and has once again demonstrated his value to the team. His attacking contributions have helped Arsenal maintain their competitive edge, making his fitness an important factor in their plans for the remainder of the campaign. The England international has established himself as one of the club’s key attacking players. Although his usual position is on the right wing, his influence across the forward line makes him difficult to replace, and Arsenal will be hoping he can recover fully before returning to action. Arsenal face another injury setback Last season, Saka and Martin Odegaard both missed numerous matches because of injuries, depriving Arsenal of two influential players for significant periods. Their improved availability this season had been encouraging, but Saka’s latest setback now threatens to disrupt the team’s progress once again. According to The Daily Mail , the winger has suffered an injury that could keep him out for up to eight weeks. The report also suggests that he may not feature for the Gunners again until the end of 2026, which would represent a considerable absence during a demanding period. Losing Saka for such a long spell would be a major concern for Arteta, who must now consider how to maintain the team’s attacking threat without one of his most dependable players. The situation also increases the importance of having sufficient depth across the forward positions. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) Arteta has alternatives to consider Despite the disappointment, Saka’s absence could create opportunities for other members of the squad to make a greater contribution. Max Dowman is expected to receive more minutes, while Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze could also come into contention for regular starting roles. Both players provide Arteta with alternative options on the wings as he looks to reorganise his attack. However, Arsenal have another fitness concern to manage, with Christos Tzolis also injured and expected to remain unavailable for several weeks. These absences could make selection more complicated, particularly if Arsenal need to rotate their attacking players across multiple competitions. item.title: Braves Make Quiet Outfield Move Before MLB Free Agency Begins
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - SEPTEMBER 11: A view of the Atlanta Braves logo on a baseball cap during the game against the Washington Nationals at Nationals Park on September 11, 2024 in Washington, DC. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) Getty Images The Atlanta Braves have some important decisions to make this offseason as they look to build on another National League East title and get closer to a return to the World Series. Injuries complicated their campaign, and their elimination from the playoffs demonstrated a need for some more pitching depth as well as more reliable offensive production, particularly from the outfield. “The Braves battled through an injury-plagued regular season to win the National League East for the seventh time in the past nine seasons,” Mark Bowman wrote for MLB.com . “But their perseverance wasn’t enough to dethrone the two-time defending World Series champion (Los Angeles) Dodgers in the NL Division Series.” Putting its pitching staff and shortstop questions aside, Atlanta will have to evaluate its outfield depth while considering how to improve the roster in free agency. But before the front office can turn its full attention to the major-league market once the World Series concludes and free agency officially begins, the Braves have already made an addition that could help their long-term plans in the outfield. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida Panthers goalie Cooper Black made history on Thursday ngiht when the puck dropped in Pittsburgh. Black, at 6-foot-9, became the tallest goalie to ever play in an NHL game and is tied as one of the tallest to ever lace up in a game. But Black’s size was just a sidebar to a bigger story: The 25-year-old, who went undrafted and signed as a free agent with the Panthers two years ago out of Dartmouth, was playing in his first NHL game. With his parents in the building, Black said he purposefully did not go searching them out in the crowd. Just playing in the NHL is tough enough. Don’t need to get all emotional and whatnot. “I know for my parents it was going to be pretty awesome,’’ Black said. “They sacrificed a lot for me to get to where I am, a lot of money and time and just overall effort. I wouldn’t be here without them. I just really appreciate what they have done for me.’’ Although Black said he “couldn’t ask for anything more,’’ in how the Panthers have welcomed him ever since he attended his first development camp in Coral Springs in 2023, they did not do him many favors in Thursday’s 4-0 loss to the Penguins. The Panthers failed to get much of anything going offensively, and Black — who gave up three goals, the final one came with him on the bench late in the third — did not get much of a chance to start his NHL career off with a win. With Jacob Markstrom thought to be out at least two weeks after getting hurt in practice Monday, there are not any obvious starts out there for the Panthers’ current backup. I think on two of their goals, they sort of waited me out a little bit. Maybe at the lower levels, they are ripping that right away. So, that’s a difference. It’s not a huge step, but a little one. By full time, Juve had lost the match, the crowd, and the argument. 2. The attack remains the biggest problem Juventus’ attacking struggles have slipped from temporary concern to a question of identity. Too often the side appears caught between ideas. Players search for passes that never arrive. Runners make movements that teammates fail to recognize. Possession circulates, but danger has not been invited to this party. The issue is not simply finishing. Juventus struggle to create consistent advantages between opposition lines. Wide players frequently receive the ball in static positions rather than dangerous ones. Too many attacks conclude before anyone in the opposition defense has genuinely felt uncomfortable. There are isolated moments of quality, but isolated moments are not a game plan. The starting lineup still contained experienced internationals and expensive talent. There was enough quality on the pitch to produce far more than Juventus ultimately showed against both Lazio and Rennes. This appears to be her time. She’s not only the best player on the Dream right now; she’s accomplished things in these Finals that are historic on an all-time and entire-league level. ANGEL REESE HISTORIC GAME 2 👑 She's just the third player in WNBA history with 30 points and 15 rebounds in a Finals game 🔥 pic.twitter.com/VpNOjq5M1h — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) October 20, 2026 Angel Reese is now the youngest player in WNBA Finals history to record 20 + points and 10 + rebounds in consecutive games. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Narrative is a funny thing in the NFL. Sometimes I question where all of the different storylines come from or why the media focuses on certain aspects over others. Not to be a conspiracy theorist (even though it’s sometimes a hobby for me), but I am sure the NFL marketing department sends information out to certain insiders to cover the stories they want to be prevailing storylines. Maybe that’s not true, but there are no definitive facts that could convince me that there isn’t a possibility that most NFL storylines portrayed in the mainstream media are contrived from somewhere inside an NFL VP or executive suite. A new narrative that could pick up steam after this weekend is that the Vikings “chose the wrong quarterback.” People are losing their minds over J.J. McCarthy coming into a game in the fourth quarter, down by 24 points, and leading a feverish comeback that ultimately felt short. It looked all too familiar to Vikings’ fans. For some reason, J.J. McCarthy has always thrived in the 4th quarter. The narrative that is already forming is that Kevin O’Connell’s system wasn’t right for McCarthy and that things are simplified in John Harbaugh’s offense. While that may be true, I didn’t see anything on Sunday that leads me to believe that McCarthy will find any more success in New York than he did in Minnesota. Jason LaCanfora is reporting that some New York Giants executive says there is going to be a major shift in offensive philosophy for New York and to look at the 2018 Ravens with Lamar Jackson in his rookie season. Apparently, New York has been eyeing McCarthy for quite some time to bring in as their starting quarterback. I find that slightly far-fetched based on them only willing to trade a 5th-round pick to acquire him. If McCarthy finds success in New York, there will be questions about why he didn’t find success in Minnesota. Persevere Toward Excellence I know what you’re thinking: STOP TALKING ABOUT THE NEW YORK GIANTS. I am, right now. Narrative lives in a world of hypotheticals. We live in the real world. Reality cannot be denied, and the Vikings are 5-0 going into a very winnable game against the Indianapolis Colts. The Minnesota Vikings have started a season with a 6-0 record six times in the modern NFL era. Of those six seasons, they made the playoffs in all but one, which was in 2003 when they lost on the last play of the season to the Arizona Cardinals. The game that culminated in the classic Paul Allen screaming “NOOOOOOOOO.” All these narratives can be squashed if Kyler Murray goes out and performs to the level at which he is capable. The experiment of drafting a first-round quarterback is over, and we are officially under the Nolan Teasley regime. Minnesota knew what they had in McCarthy. Maybe the Giants were willing to give more in a trade, but the narrative that I am choosing to perpetuate is that the front office was simply ready to move on and was satisfied getting any value back. I wish J.J. the best, but the franchise has chosen a new path. That is what I will do here as well and move on. The Minnesota Vikings are the most enigmatic team in the NFL. Some armchair NFL analysts (people on social media who bought a microphone and know how to post on the internet) are saying that the Vikings are the third-best team in the NFC North. They’re not calling us the third-best 5-0 team; they are saying that the Bears and Packers (both of whom we beat with Carson Wentz) are better. HA! Are We Witnessing History? This defense is special. Like really special, as evidenced by how the Vikings’ current 10-game win streak has manifested itself. Over the last 10 games, the Minnesota Vikings have scored 229 points. Historically, you have to go back to 1934 to find a 10-game winning streak where the team scored fewer points (the 1934 Detroit Lions scored 215 points). That is an astonishing statistic but speaks to the dominance that we have seen from this defense. Football is about winning games. Sure, the Vikings offense has had its struggles and is still finding its footing. Is that a circumstance of poor coaching or them being a bad offense? Or is it a result of a shift in philosophy for Kevin O’Connell? From a narrative perspective, KO is rewriting the defining story of his time as the coach of the Minnesota Vikings. He recently talked about how he has shifted his mindset from being concerned with what stats look like on paper to winning football games. This team is playing complementary football at its finest. Every season has its ebbs and flows, but we also see those differences happen over the course of multiple seasons. Right now, the defense is obviously the strength of this team. When Brian Flores’ unit is fresh, they are almost unstoppable. One thing I have noticed is just how relentless the defensive front is. They just keep coming and don’t stop until after the whistle. The defense is playing with such an intensity that it simply wears down opposing offenses and beats them down into submission. Gotta Have the Ball to Score An important factor in this success is the offense’s ability to maintain drives. So far this season, the Vikings’ are averaging the second highest average time of possession in the league at 33:38 per game. They trail only the Chicago Bears in this category. I will concede that the Vikings haven’t been very efficient when it comes to scoring touchdowns, but I firmly believe that is going to change. In fantasy football, we talk about regression toward the mean. The Minnesota offense has only scored eight offensive touchdowns in 5 games played this season, which is the 2nd fewest in the league. However, this offense is better than that, and we will start to see that number look more normal going forward. Another prevailing shift in philosophy is that this now appears to be a run-first offense, as evidenced by the aforementioned time of possession statistic. This offense is about controlling the clock and taking care of the football. It’s like we are time traveling back to the Mike Zimmer era. However, this is the Teasley/O’Connell/Flores era. We are fans of one of the premier organizations in the NFL, and I think we are going to actually see success beyond the regular season. I know, as a Vikings fan, hope is a slippery slope. A slippery slope to sadness and disappointment. There Is a Long Road Ahead The game this Sunday against the Colts will set the tone for the rest of the season. I fully expect Indianapolis, with their backs to the wall, to make this game competitive for as long as they can. I can also see Daniel Jones throwing four interceptions, which would squash a different narrative that the Vikings shouldn’t have let him leave the building. I think Minnesota wins this game in dominant fashion, and we see our offense come to life. They are going to have to, because this team has a tough schedule going forward where they are going to have to put some points on the board. It’s time for this offense to get rolling and for the defense to keep doing what it does. I can’t wait for Sunday! Until Next Skol.

item.title: INTERVIEW | Charlie Cresswell on Rennes’ Europa League goals: ‘There are no limits.’
item.description: INTERVIEW | Charlie Cresswell on Rennes’ Europa League goals: ‘There are no limits.’ Stade Rennais head to Turin tonight in what is their biggest challenge so far in this season’s UEFA Europa League. Thus far, Rennes have one win and one draw in the competition. Speaking to Get French Football News, Charlie Cresswell (23) outlined the Breton club’s objectives in the competition. The former England youth international said that participating in European competition was part of the draw at Rennes. Tonight’s match against Juventus is the highlight fixture in their ‘League Phase’ draw. Speaking ahead of it, Cresswell outlined the objectives. “There are no limits. It would be stupid to put limits on ourselves. We can say we can win it.” He added, “[We have] such a good team here, good staff. Yeah, it’d be stupid to put limits on ourselves. ” In what is the first European campaign of Cresswell’s young career, he is not just there to make up the numbers. item.title: Real Madrid consider activating €80 million buyback clause for Nico Paz in 2027 – report
item.description: Real Madrid consider activating €80 million buyback clause for Nico Paz in 2027 – report Real Madrid are reportedly considering bringing Nico Paz back to the club in 2027 by activating an €80 million buy-back clause, according to Spanish journalist Ramon Alvarez . The Argentine attacking midfielder has made significant progress at Como under Cesc Fabregas, strengthening the case for a potential return to the Santiago Bernabeu. Real Madrid eye Nico Paz return from Como Real Madrid have begun looking ahead to the 2027/28 campaign, assessing potential reinforcements, particularly in defence and midfield. The Merengues are also monitoring former academy players who have developed impressively after leaving Madrid. And Nico Paz is one of the most prominent examples. The Argentine has continued to enhance his reputation at Como, where he has developed under former Barcelona midfielder Fabregas. Excelling at Como. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) His performances have reportedly kept Real Madrid interested in bringing him back, with Ramon Alvarez claiming that the club want to exercise the €80 million buyback option for the Argentine playmaker. The reported fee would represent a substantial investment in a player the Spanish giants already know from their academy system. Real Madrid re-signed Nico Paz this past summer only to sell him back to Como as the youngster sought to continue his development at Como rather than returning to the Santiago Bernabeu. The decision has proved to be the right one as the 22-year-old Argentine playmaker has excelled for Como, managing four goals and five assists in ten games. Will Nico Paz return to Real Madrid in 2027? (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) As part of the new agreement, the Spanish capital club retained another buyback option worth €80 million for 2027. Nico Paz faces a potential midfield selection dilemma at Real Madrid Paz’s progress at Como gives Real Madrid a compelling reason to consider bringing him back, but finding him a regular role could prove complicated. Real Madrid already have considerable competition in attacking midfield, with Jude Bellingham a leading option in the position. Arda Guler also offers an alternative, creating a potential selection challenge if Paz returns. The club would therefore need to weigh the Argentine’s growing potential against the demands of building a balanced squad. After all, substantial investment would naturally bring expectations around his playing time and role within the team.

item.title: New British number one Boulter loses Japan semi-final
item.description: Katie Boulter's last WTA title came at the Ostrava Open in February [Getty Images] Katie Boulter has lost in the Japan Open semi-finals, in her first match since reclaiming the British number one spot from Sonny Kartal. Kartal moved above Boulter in the world rankings by reaching the final of last week's Wuhan Open. But Boulter's run to the last four in Osaka, which included a victory over Antonia Ruzic in the quarter-finals, will be enough for her to go back above Kartal when the rankings are next updated. However, the 30-year-old missed the chance to reach the final, and a shot at a fifth WTA singles title, losing 6-1 6-4 to doubles world number one Siniakova. Eighth seed Boulter rallied after being swept aside in the opening set, going a break up at the start of the second. But Siniakova, also 30, maintained her bid for a first singles title in four years by claiming two hard-fought breaks of her own to wrap up victory in 85 minutes. She will now play 2023 champion Ashlyn Krueger in Sunday's final after the 22-year-old American beat compatriot and top seed Ann Li 6-4 6-7 (4-7) 6-3. item.description: Man Utd urging patience with summer signing who ‘struggled’ in Como – Will he prove doubters wrong? Manchester United are placing high hopes on Tynan Thompson, despite his early struggles at Carrington. The Premier League giants had an excessively quiet summer transfer campaign. They almost exclusively focused on the midfield revamp, signing Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, and Carlos Baleba. The only other first-team arrival was backup goalkeeper Karl Darlow. Nevertheless, INEOS made a few interesting moves in the youth section, and chief among them was Thompson . Man Utd back Tynan Thompson to prove naysayers wrong (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) The 18-year-old is considered among the most exciting teenagers in the country after his exploits with Tottenham’s U21 side last season. Unlike other youngsters who were poached for free, Man Utd were happy to spend £8 million to secure Thompson’s services. The left winger was initially tipped to play a hybrid role between United’s U21 side and Michael Carrick’s first team, offering additional depth behind Matheus Cunha, Marcus Rashford, and Patrick Dorgu. However, the early Carabao Cup elimination will hamper his chances of earning minutes. The London native has yet to make his senior debut, with no signs on the horizon. On Wednesday, Thompson started for Man Utd’s U19 team, which took on Como U19 in the UEFA Youth League. While the young Reds didn’t suffer a heavy defeat like the seniors later in the day, they still returned home empty-handed after losing 1-2 to their Italian hosts. Jack Fletcher’s second-half goal wasn’t enough to spark a comeback. According to The Sun journalists Katherine Walsh and Samuel Luckhurst, Thompson ‘struggled’ in his outing against Como. The winger’s performances are beginning to draw criticism from fans and observers. Nevertheless, Man Utd still believe in the teenager’s talent, tipping him to overcome his early difficulties and become an added asset to the first team at some point. All judgement on Thompson should be postponed (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Unfortunately for Thompson, he finds himself at a club engulfed by a toxic atmosphere. Even the youth sector has had its fair share of the drama, with JJ Gabriel refusing to play and trying to force his way out of the club. If the most talented players in the senior squad haven’t been able to find their footing since the start of the season, one can hardly blame a teenager for playing below his level, especially while he’s still adjusting to his new surroundings. Moreover, the metrics above prove he hasn’t been as lacklustre as some are trying to paint him, as he’s been able to provide his teammates with three assists. However, the early Carabao Cup elimination will hamper his chances of earning minutes. The London native has yet to make his senior debut, with no signs on the horizon. On Wednesday, Thompson started for Man Utd’s U19 team, which took on Como U19 in the UEFA Youth League. While the young Reds didn’t suffer a heavy defeat like the seniors later in the day, they still returned home empty-handed after losing 1-2 to their Italian hosts. Jack Fletcher’s second-half goal wasn’t enough to spark a comeback. According to The Sun journalists Katherine Walsh and Samuel Luckhurst, Thompson ‘struggled’ in his outing against Como. The winger’s performances are beginning to draw criticism from fans and observers. Even the youth sector has had its fair share of the drama, with JJ Gabriel refusing to play and trying to force his way out of the club. If the most talented players in the senior squad haven’t been able to find their footing since the start of the season, one can hardly blame a teenager for playing below his level, especially while he’s still adjusting to his new surroundings. Moreover, the metrics above prove he hasn’t been as lacklustre as some are trying to paint him, as he’s been able to provide his teammates with three assists. Barcelona won their first 11 games of the season in all competitions before Paris Saint-Germain beat them 4-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday. Real Madrid’s 4-1 win over Sevilla last Sunday, with two goals from Kylian Mbappé, cut Barcelona’s lead at the top of LaLiga to six points, but a home win on Sunday would put Barcelona nine points clear. Despite defeats already this season to Real Betis and Atlético Madrid, Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4-1 at the Bernabéu on Wednesday for a third win from three in the Champions League, after victories over Inter and Roma. Mourinho dismissed the idea that the Paris result would rattle Barcelona, saying, “I don’t think losing one match will change his state of mind or his confidence. Nor would it have changed me if we’d lost 4-1 to Leipzig.” He also pushed back on the comparison between the two squads. “We’re seen as a finished product, and that’s very difficult in football, but we’re not at an advanced stage of that process; we’ve been working for three months, with a pre-season where players were arriving in pairs each week, then the break,” he said. “Comparing a team at this stage with one that’s been together for several years doesn’t seem fair to me.” Questions about Barcelona coach Hansi Flick got shorter answers. “I don’t understand the questions about our opponents. What do you want me to say?” “Real Madrid win trophies with Mourinho” The sharpest line came when he was asked whether Sunday was a test of whether this Real Madrid team could win titles. “No,” he said. “Real Madrid win trophies with Mourinho.” His Clásico record from his first spell is less emphatic than that answer. Between 2010-11 and 2012-13, Mourinho’s Madrid met Barcelona 17 times across LaLiga, the Copa del Rey, the Champions League and the Supercopa. They won five, drew six and lost six. The first of those games is the one Barcelona fans still bring up, when Mourinho arrived at Camp Nou in November 2010 having made the best start of any Real Madrid coach in history, UEFA noted, and was unbeaten in his first 19 games. Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona won 5-0 and Mourinho called it the heaviest defeat of his career. It was also his first return to the stadium where he had worked as Bobby Robson’s translator in the 1990s. The spring of 2011 brought four Clásicos in 18 days. Before the league meeting, Mourinho skipped the pre-match press conference and sent assistant Aitor Karanka in his place, prompting a walkout by some journalists. He did the same before the December 2011 Clásico, although this Saturday, he faced the room himself. That April run produced his first win over Guardiola, 1-0 after extra time in the Copa del Rey final in Valencia, settled by a Cristiano Ronaldo header. A week later came the Champions League semi-final first leg at the Bernabéu. Madrid lost 2-0, Mourinho was sent to the stands. The low point arrived at the end of the Supercopa at Camp Nou in August 2011, when Mourinho poked Barcelona assistant Tito Vilanova in the eye during a touchline brawl. By January 2012, after a 2-2 Copa draw in Barcelona, he was claiming it was impossible to win there. Three months later he did. Madrid won 2-1 at Camp Nou in April 2012, with Ronaldo scoring the winner. The result ended Barcelona’s run of 55 home games unbeaten and effectively secured Madrid’s first league title in four years. Mourinho finished his first spell unbeaten in his last five Clásicos, including a 3-1 Copa semi-final win at Camp Nou in February 2013. That is the record he leaned on years later, when asked about his poor numbers against Guardiola. “I won the match for the title in Barcelona with Real Madrid,” he told reporters. Saturday’s answer about trophies came from the same place. Mourinho played down any special significance in the venue. “It’s just like playing at a different stadium. We’re talking about a very strong side. But it’s no big deal.” He was happier talking about the fixture itself. “There are other important derbies in the world, but this is the one and only Clásico, the world comes to a standstill,” he said. On Sunday, the world will stop to take in one of soccer’s greatest rivalries as Barcelona host Real Madrid at Spotify Camp Nou at 9pm local time (3pm ET) on Sunday, October 25. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
